 JUDGMENT
The Police sub Inspector of Malleswaram police station has filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable Under Secs. 420, 468, 471 and 120(B) of IPC.
2. The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:

That the accused hatched a plan to make wrongful monetary gain from the Karnataka State Government and created and registered a bogus and parallel association by name Bangalore Urban Zilla Amateur Kabaddi Association.

Thereafter the investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation,
the IO has submitted the charge sheet against the accused for the offences U/s 120(B), 420, 468, 471 of IPC.
4.

Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the matter was posted for evidence.

6. I have heard the arguments addressed by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned advocate for the accused.

On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :
POINTS 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that in between 29.02.2020 and 17.06.2020 the accused hatched a plan to make wrongful monetary gain from the Karnataka State Government and created and registered a bogus and parallel association by name Bangalore Urban Zilla Amateur Kabaddi Association and thereby the accused has committed an offence of "criminal conspiracy"
punishable U/Sec.120(B) of IPC ?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused on 29.02.2020 forged the documents relating to registration of the bogus Bangalore Urban Zilla Amateur Kabaddi Association and forged the signatures of the Vice President of Bangalore Urban District Amateur Kabaddi Association and thereby the accused has committed an offence of "forgery for the purpose of cheating" punishable U/Sec.468 of IPC ?

sentences.text:
My findings to the above Points are as under:
Point No.1 to 4 : In the Negative.
 Point No.5 :

As per final order,
 For the following: -
 REASONS 10. Point No.1 to 4:-

As these points are interlinked with each other and also similar evidence is led on all these points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order C.C.13523/2021 to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.
11. It is allegation that the accused has committed the offences punishable under Section 120(B), 468, 471 and 420 of Indian Penal Code.
12. In order to prove its case, prosecution has got examined C.W.2/V.Jayaram as P.W.1, C.W.3/Y.M.Balaji Venkatesh as P.W2 and informant of crime/C.W.1 by name Suresh Gowda as P.W.3.

Out of the documents marked for the prosecution Ex.P.1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the mahazar,
Ex.P.3 is the complaint, Ex.P.4-is the mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the complaint, Ex.P.6 is the spot mahazar and Ex.P.7 is the statement of P.W.3.
During the course of cross examination of PW1 he got confronted and got marked document as Ex.D1.
Ex.D1 is the proceedings of meeting.
13. Initially PW1 and 2 have supported the case of prosecution and counsel for accused cross examined the witnesses at length.

14. During their cross examination P.W.1 and 2 being the prime witnesses turned fully hostile to the case of the prosecution C.C.13523/2021 in the lengthy cross-examination made by learned counsel for accused and the PW1 and 2 deposed in their cross examination that they did not lodge complaint against the accused and police did not draw mahazar and they do not know the contents of the Ex.P.1 to 4 and further deposed that due to oversight they deposed the evidence against the accused on 09.09.2022, 30.09.2022, 09.12.2022, 15.02.2023, 07.06.2023 and 24.08.2023.
Nothing worth has been elicited from their mouth to support the case of the prosecution.
During their cross examination by learned APP they deposed that they have compromised the matter with the accused.
Suresh Gowda in his chief examination has deposed that he knows the accused.
He has no knowledge about this case and he has not lodged complaint to the police and the police took his signatures on blank paper.
He does not know the contents of Ex.P.5-Complaint and police have not drawn mahazar as per Ex.P.6 and he does not know the contents of the mahazar which is at Ex.P.6.

sentences.text: The P.W.3 being the prime witness turned fully hostile to the case of the prosecution.
In the lengthy cross-examination of PW.3 C.C.13523/2021 made by learned Sr.A.P.P, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth to support the case of the prosecution.
He denied the suggestion that he has lodged complaint as per Ex.P.5 and police has drawn mahazar as per Ex.P.6.
He denied the suggestion that he is deposing false evidence since he has compromised the matter with the accused.

16. Now on over all perusal of the evidence of the prosecution witnesses , it is evident to note that PW1 to 3 being the material witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution in cross examination made by the counsel for accused.
The PW.1 and 2 prime witnesses denied the entire case of the prosecution in the cross examination made by Learned Counsel for accused and also turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
The PW1 to 3 denied the involvement of the accused and at the out set they have denied the entire case of the prosecution, as they have settled the matter with the accused.
17. However, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor prays to issue summons to other witnesses.

Having considered the facts and circumstances of this case, this court was of the opinion that even if C.C.13523/2021 other witnesses were examined, it would be a futile exercise and no lawful purpose would have been served.

As such examination of the prosecution witnesses only for the purpose of completing the procedural aspect and will not serve any judicial purpose and it is sheer waste of the precious time of the court.
Therefore, the prayer of the learned APP to issue summons to other witnesses was rejected.

At this stage this court relied upon judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration & another: wherein at page No.13 the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date".

entities.text: 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case is applicable in this case also.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the above Point Nos.1 to 4 are answered in the 'NEGATIVE'.

C.C.13523/2021 18. Point No.5: - In view of the findings of point No.1 to 4 this court proceeds to pass the following;-
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused is acquitted of the offence punishable U/Sec.120(B),
468, 471 and 420 of Indian Penal Code.
Bail bonds of the accused and Surety bond shall stand canceled.
The bail bond executed U/Sec.437(A) of Cr.P.C shall be continued.
